officialInventory.summary: Wildlife protected areas are managed by the Wildlife Division of the Forestry Commission and are legally established by the Wildlife Reserves Regulations 1971 (L.I. 710) and its amendments (kept in force by the Wildlife Resources Management Act 2023, Act 1115). The NBSAP (Nov 2016, Table 4, source FDMP 2016) gives the most complete official list with areas and years. Forest reserves (~280) are managed by the Forest Services Division and were not enumerated. The Forestry Commission website was not used (reported hijacked/dead).

statedCounts.category: legally-constituted wildlife conservation areas incl. Ramsar sites
statedCounts.quote: There are 21 legally-constituted wildlife conservation areas, notably six national parks, six resource reserves, three wildlife sanctuaries, one strict nature reserve as well as six Ramsar Sites
Currently, there are 280 forest reserves in Ghana

gaps: Counts conflict: NBSAP text says six national parks and three sanctuaries while its Table 4 lists seven national parks and three gazetted sanctuaries (+1 proposed); the 6NR says 7 NP, 6 RR, 2 WS, 1 SNR. Records follow Table 4.
Legal instruments for Kyabobo NP, Boabeng-Fiema WS and the original Bia NP gazette (L.I. 881, 1974) and L.I. 1283 (1983) were not seen.
The NBSAP mentions one proposed national park whose name is not given.
No Ghanaian marine protected area was found in official sources.
